profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.profile: This is the kind of golf that makes pars feel like a charity donation. The recurring crime scene is the flatstick: enough missed damage around the greens to turn decent looks into three-jack therapy sessions, while the approach play keeps kicking the door open just long enough for the rest of the bag to set it on fire. There are flashes where the tee game shows up, but they never stay long enough to bail out the short game mess. When the scoring gets ugly, it’s usually because the whole chain snaps in the same round.

profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.profile: This file is pure golf whiplash: the irons can absolutely cook, then the rest of the bag strolls in wearing a ski mask. The profile keeps circling back to a player who can create birdie looks and still manage to make the round feel like a hostage situation with the driver and short game. There’s enough competence tee to green to explain why the good rounds happen, but the bad ones get dragged down by enough self-inflicted nonsense to make the whole thing look unstable. The identity is real; the ceiling just keeps getting mugged.

profiles.name: TEV_11
profiles.profile: This one lives on the weird edge between hope and arson. When the driver behaves, the rest of the game can look perfectly playable, but the iron play has also produced some absolute nonsense that nukes good starts in a hurry. The profile says there’s actual upside here, yet it shows up wearing a fake mustache and leaves before the round can trust it. Good tee-ball energy, enough short-game competence to survive, and then the approach game occasionally rips the steering wheel out and sends the car into the ditch.

profiles.name: tnboles77
profiles.profile: This dude is basically a rescue mission from 30 yards and in. The clearest repeatable trait is that the short game keeps dragging him back from the ledge, which is funny because the tee and approach numbers keep trying to throw him straight off it. The long clubs are a mess often enough that the rounds can look cooked, but there’s enough around-the-green competence to keep him alive when the rest of the bag is acting like it got locked in a shed. That’s a volatile profile, but not a dead one.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.profile: This bag has real heat and no sense of responsibility. When it’s on, there’s enough pop and enough putter to steal a round; when it’s off, the short game and tee-to-green stuff conspire like they’ve got a grudge. The identity here is less “clean striker” and more “volatile shot-maker who can absolutely win you one and then faceplant the next day.” The weird part is the putter occasionally bails out the mess, which is almost rude, because the rest of the profile keeps handing it sandbags and excuses to fail.

profiles.name: Jakobm90
profiles.profile: This profile is a roller coaster somebody built with a blindfold on. The driver can show real life, but the approach play has also had some absolutely brutal stretches, and when that happens the whole round starts bleeding out fast. There’s enough scoring upside to prove the talent is in there, but the volatility is loud as hell: one round the ball is flying, the next it’s a full-on compass malfunction. The good news is the player can create a proper spike week; the bad news is the floor keeps trying to eat the ceiling.
